messages:
alex_chen: Heads up — config-only deploy planned for tonight 00:30 UTC. Changes: routing policy tweak + batching params + token timeout. Canary at 5% for 15m, then 25% if no regressions. No code changes. Anyone see compliance/regressions risk?

maria_g: sounds fine. pls add explicit pin fallback to previous routing profile if p95 latency + error rate exceed thresholds. also include release notes snippet.

alex_chen: will do. proposed thresholds: p95 latency increase > 15% OR error rate > 0.5% => rollback/pin. does that sound reasonable?

samir: +1 on thresholds. also recommend a short change window (30m) to watch cache warming effects. batching change might spike CPU initially.

leo: Where are we routing small vs large requests now? Need snippet for ops playbook.

alex_chen: current -> new routing rule (canary):
```
route_rules:
  - name: small-reqs-low-latency
    match: request_tokens <= 128
    target_pool: low-latency
    weight: 0.05
  - name: default
    match: else
    target_pool: standard
    weight: 0.95
batching:
  target_batch_size: 32
  max_wait_ms: 120
token_timeout_ms: 120
```
I'll attach this to the deploy.

deploy-bot: Config deploy scheduled by @alex_chen for 2026-03-20T00:30:00Z. Canary: 5% (routing + batching). Change ID: cfg-20260320-7.

maria_g: add rollback instructions to the release notes: "cfg-20260320-7 can be reverted via pinning routing_profile=cfg-20260307-v3 in the console or invoking ops-tool rollback --change cfg-20260320-7"

alex_chen: done. release notes drafted and pushed to the changelog draft.

ops_oncall: I'll be on watch for the 00:30 window. If we see p95 > 650ms or errors > 0.5% I'll either pin back or revert the routing policy immediately. Please @mention me in the deploy channel.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout started at 2026-03-20T00:30:00Z for cfg-20260320-7 -> 5% traffic.

alex_chen: monitoring set up: dashboards for p50/p95, cpu_util, error_rate; alert rule tagged with cfg-20260320-7.

deploy-bot: Canary metrics after 10m: p50 120ms (+5%), p95 720ms (+20%), error_rate 0.6% (up). Flags: p95 > threshold, error_rate > threshold.

samir: seeing increased tail latency on low-latency pool. suspect batching backpressure due to smaller per-instance capacity.

leo: can we pin routing_profile to previous stable: routing_profile=stable-20260301 while we investigate?

alex_chen: recommend immediate PIN to be safe. rolling forward will reduce customer impact. Who can execute?

ops_oncall: I'll run the pin now. Executing: ops-tool pin --profile stable-20260301 --change cfg-20260320-7 --reason "p95 & errors regressed"

deploy-bot: Pin applied at 2026-03-20T00:45:12Z. All traffic routed to routing_profile=stable-20260301. cfg-20260320-7 marked 'paused'.

maria_g: thanks. update release notes: mark cfg-20260320-7 as "paused due to tail latency regression; follow-up: investigate batching kernel and pool sizing". Add ticket: INF-4123.

alex_chen: created INF-4123 and assigned to eng-runtime. Added reproducer logs and sample traces.

samir: initial hypothesis: target_batch_size 32 causes longer queue times on certain GPU instances when concurrent KV cache pressure is high. I'll run local repro with current load profile.

leo: ops follow-up: consider temporary capacity bump on low-latency pool for the next 48h while we test smaller batch sizes or adaptive batching.

ops_oncall: noted. bumped low-latency pool by +10% capacity at 2026-03-20T01:05:00Z as precaution.

alex_chen: thanks everyone. Action items: ENG-RUNTIME (samir) investigate INF-4123; ops to keep capacity bump until test complete; release notes updated with pause/rollback + pin steps; recreate canary with smaller batch_size (16) in a new change once root cause validated.

maria_g: good postmortem plan. we'll re-schedule config-only retry in the next change window after tests. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Thread closed for cfg-20260320-7 (paused)."
